facts.statement: The genus Eopteranodon was named in 2005 by paleontologists Lü Junchang and Zhang Xingliao.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2005 by paleontologists Lü Junchang and Zhang Xingliao.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Eopteranodon lii.
facts.quote: The type species is Eopteranodon lii.

facts.statement: Eopteranodon had a toothless skull featuring a large crest that was similar to that of Pteranodon.
facts.quote: Its skull, including a large crest, was toothless and similar to that of Pteranodon.

facts.statement: A second specimen, D2526, described in 2006, possessed a larger wingspan than the type specimen.
facts.quote: A second specimen, D2526, described in 2006, had a larger wingspan.

facts.statement: In 2017, a phylogenetic analysis classified Eopteranodon as a member of the family Tapejaridae based on crest and limb proportions.
facts.quote: Later, in 2017, in another phylogenetic analysis, Eopteranodon was considered a member of the family Tapejaridae based on proportions of the crest on the lower jaw and the limbs.

facts.statement: Some classifications place Eopteranodon within the family Chaoyangopteridae.
Eopteranodon lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: A second species, E. yixianensis, was named in 2023, though its validity remains questioned by scientists.
facts.quote: A second species, E. yixianensis, was named in 2023, but its validity has been questioned.
